01 · The Competition

What Is Science Olympiad?

Science Olympiad is a national STEM competition where teams of students compete across events spanning life science, earth & space science, physical science, engineering, and inquiry — through written tests, hands-on labs, and built devices.

Division A

At Haycock, our 3rd, 4th, and 5th graders compete here.

Division B

Nationally grades 6–9. At Haycock, our 5th and 6th graders compete in Division B. They face middle school teams almost entirely composed of 8th and 9th graders.

A 5th grader may compete in Division A or Division B — not both in the same year. This is a one-team commitment.

04 · The Format

How Division B Works

15
students on each team
23
events to cover, every one required
3–4
events per student — most do 3, three students per team take on 4
2
students represent Haycock at most events — rarely 3

Students are paired up for each event and prepare together — sharing the workload, the study time, and the credit.

05 · Time & Effort

Not A Drop-Off Activity

Students

At least 2 hours a week, per event, studying together. Complex written events and builds routinely take longer to get good at.

Parents

Every family mentors 1–2 events. That means making sure your kids are prepared — folders and cheat sheets ready, studying and teaching alongside them, running practice tests. Volunteering matters just as much, both to help the team and at tournaments themselves — teams that don't sign up to volunteer are not allowed to attend regionals or States.

This only works if parents mentor. Please plan for that before you apply.

08 · Communicating Event Preferences

Sorting Into Events

Option A

Rank preferred event groups — pre-set pairings of events students take on together as a set. This is the method we'll most likely use.

Option B

We also collect your top 6 individual events — in case enrollment numbers mean we need to adjust group assignments.

We'll most likely sort by event groups this season — final enrollment numbers and the 5th/6th grade ratio could still change that. Either way, we ask for both on the Student Intake Form.

09 · What Happens Next

Interest Isn't The Commitment

Sharing your email with us today just tells us you're interested. Every family who does will receive a Student Intake Form — and completing that is the real commitment to participate.

The 2027 event rules are now available — download them at soinc.org/rules-2027. When downloading, select "Parent," not "Coach."
